questions.question: In an investigation, nobody knows in advance which checks will be needed. What makes a fixed orchestrator plan awkward here?
options: The next step depends on what earlier steps find, so the plan would have to be rewritten constantly
questions.explanation: A blackboard lets the order of work emerge from the data.

questions.question: How does an agent on a blackboard decide when to act?
options: Its trigger checks the board for entries it can use
questions.explanation: Agents don't call each other; they react to the board.

questions.question: Adding deploy_watcher changed the conclusion from 'pool exhausted' to 'bad deploy leaks connections'. What code changed in the other agents?
options: None; the new agent's entries gave existing agents more to work with
questions.explanation: Extensibility without rewiring is the pattern's main strength.

questions.question: Two agents read version 1 of an entry and both write changes. With blind writes, what happens?
options: The second write silently erases the first (a lost update)
questions.explanation: Versioned writes turn the second write into a conflict that's retried on fresh data.

questions.question: Why does every entry carry based_on links?
options: So any conclusion can be traced back to observed facts and who posted them
questions.explanation: With many writers, provenance is how you tell evidence from invention.

questions.question: What's the main risk of a blackboard compared with an orchestrator?
options: The order of work is harder to predict, and without stop conditions agents can keep acting forever
It needs one model per agent
questions.explanation: Design the control loop's stop conditions as carefully as the entry types.
